correctness.rationale: For each private-leaf pair, weight one forces empty original/singleton leaf; the independent indices of such pairs are bounded by the cycle independence number. Equality forces exactly a maximum independent set of empty originals and five explicit weight-two pair types on its complement. For any zero original, its leaf has one choice when the two neighboring core states coincide in a pure color and two choices otherwise. This gives the exact 3-state transfer matrix. A cycle of m constraints appears for even orders, and a path of m constraints appears in each of n maximum independent sets for odd orders. Symmetric and antisymmetric matrix decomposition proves the displayed closed forms and recurrence. Direct all-labeling exhaustive computation on orders 3..6 independently verifies 17,895,424 assignments; arithmetic checks continue through order 51. No extrapolation of finite data is used.

originality.rationale: The two pertinent 2022 primary articles were examined at full-text level. Samadi–Soltankhah Theorem 3.4 (arXiv:2208.02340, pp. 10–11) determines exactly the already-known scalar optimum 2n-alpha(C_n) of a one-leaf corona but neither enumerates the labeled optimum functions nor gives the displayed matrix/path/trace formula. Cabrera-Martínez 2022 Theorem 6 treats scalar corona results when both factors lack isolated vertices and hence does not apply to the one-leaf second factor; it contains no optimum-function census. Searches of other related parameters and public mathematical records identified no equivalent optimum-count result. There is residual priority uncertainty in unindexed work.
residual_risks: The scalar-one-leaf-corona proof of Samadi–Soltankhah already supplies necessary equality restrictions, though not the explicit optimum counts; the gain is an exact enumeration refinement.
An unindexed article, thesis appendix, integer-sequence table or independent implementation could already contain the same sunlet optimum counts.
No expert or independent audit has been performed, and complete bibliographic priority is not certified.

value.rationale: For a natural, infinite cycle-with-leaf family, the optimum number is known, but the count and structure of all named-color minimum configurations are a separate natural combinatorial invariant. The finding gives a complete solution of that census, including parity-split cyclic versus path transfer products, a closed even formula, and a low-order odd recurrence. It reveals the exact degree of flexibility among optimally weighted assignments, with potential use in enumeration and sampling. No unmotivated parameter slice, relabeling, or routine restatement of the scalar optimum is presented.
